overview: Three-month, full-time (≈7 h/day) accelerated plan that covers fundamentals and critical applied backend skills: Python, core CS (data structures, OOP, debugging), version control, relational databases, API design with FastAPI, testing, containerization, CI, and a hands-on integration project. Each month is focused and project-driven so you practice building a deployable backend while preserving time for interview practice and communication skills.

topics: Python syntax, data types, variables, control flow, functions, modules
Basic I/O, file handling, error handling (try/except)
Lists, dictionaries, basic stacks/queues concepts, Big O basics
Classes & objects, encapsulation, simple class methods
Using IDE/editor, breakpoints, inspect variables, effective logging/prints for debugging
Git: add/commit/push/pull, branching and merging basics, resolving simple conflicts
GitHub: repo creation, cloning, PR workflow and issues basics
SQL: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, WHERE/GROUP BY/ORDER BY, JOIN basics
PostgreSQL: install, psql basics, create DB/tables, basic CRUD, connect via a client
objectives: Be fluent in writing and reading Python scripts and small programs.
Implement and analyze basic data structures and know when to use them.
Write simple classes and apply basic OOP patterns.
Debug programs using IDE/debugger and logging/prints.
Use Git and GitHub for source control and collaborative workflows.
Write and run core SQL queries and operate a local PostgreSQL instance.
projects: Mini-project A: CLI-based data processor in Python that reads CSV, processes data (using lists/dicts), and writes output. Include unit tests for core functions.
Repository setup: Initialize project repo on GitHub, use branches for feature work and open a PR to merge to main.
resources: Official Python tutorial + interactive exercises (e.g., exercism.io, LeetCode easy problems)
Automated Git tutorials (e.g., Git SCM book, GitHub Learning Lab)
PostgreSQL quickstart guides and psql cheatsheet
Short course: Python for Everybody or similar (first modules)
Debugging guide for your chosen IDE (VS Code / PyCharm)

topics: HTTP methods, status codes, headers, request/response modeling, authentication concepts (API keys/JWT overview)
REST principles: resource design, idempotency, status usage, endpoint design
FastAPI: routes, path/query params, request body validation with Pydantic, dependency injection basics
Connecting FastAPI to PostgreSQL (SQLAlchemy or async DB drivers) for CRUD endpoints
Write unit tests using pytest: assertions, fixtures, mocking external dependencies
Dockerfile basics, building images, running containers, bind mounts for local development
Design APIs using OOP patterns for maintainability (separation of concerns)
objectives: Design and implement RESTful endpoints with FastAPI and validate inputs with Pydantic.
Integrate application with PostgreSQL for persistent storage and perform migrations/basic schema changes.
Write reliable unit tests and use fixtures and mocks for isolated testing.
Containerize the application for local reproducible environments.
Follow REST best practices and structure code for maintainability.
projects: Mini-project B: Build a small RESTful FastAPI service (e.g., task manager or notes app) with PostgreSQL backend, validated request models, and a test suite covering core endpoints.
Dockerize the service with a simple Dockerfile and run it locally with a PostgreSQL container (use docker-compose or separate containers).
resources: FastAPI official docs and tutorial (path/query params, Pydantic examples)
SQLAlchemy or async DB driver quickstarts; Alembic basics for migrations (optional overview)
Pytest documentation and example guides; small TDD exercises
Docker getting-started guide and Dockerfile best practices articles
REST API design checklist and HTTP status code reference

skills_focus: Caching concept overview (light Redis intro, conceptual)
topics: Compose an end-to-end app: API, DB, tests, and Docker workflow
Set up GitHub Actions to run tests on push and PR; automate linting and basic checks
Basic logging (structured logs, log levels) and simple metrics (request count, error rate)
Caching: why and where it helps (read-through/write-through), conceptual Redis use for response caching or sessions
CI pipeline for building image, running tests, and optionally pushing to a container registry
Targeted algorithm & DS practice focused on interview-style problems (decomposition, complexity, whiteboard practice)
Practicing clear written documentation (README, API docs) and short technical presentations
objectives: Deliver a reproducible, containerized FastAPI application with automated tests and CI checks.
Understand basic operational concerns (logging and simple monitoring metrics) and where caching fits.
Be able to explain design decisions, demonstrate the app, and communicate clearly in writing and short demos.
Perform focused interview problem-solving practice and articulate solutions, trade-offs, and complexity.
projects: Capstone Project: Complete and polish the Dockerized FastAPI app from Month 2. Add CI with GitHub Actions (run tests + lint). Prepare README, API usage examples, and demo script.
Optional add-on (time permitting): Integrate basic Redis caching for one read endpoint and show cache invalidation strategy.
resources: GitHub Actions documentation and starter workflows for Python projects
Guides on containerizing & local deployment (docker-compose for multi-container stacks)
Logging libraries (structlog or Python logging config) examples and Sentry/Prometheus conceptual docs
Redis quickstart and FastAPI-Redis integration examples (if attempted)
Interview prep platforms (LeetCode, AlgoExpert, Pramp) with curated problem sets focusing on arrays, hashes, linked lists, trees
Templates for README & API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger from FastAPI)

tips: Treat Sundays (or the last day of your study week) as a light day for review, consolidation, and planning next week; do shallow bakes rather than new heavy topics.
Keep one single GitHub repository active across months for your capstone; it becomes a living portfolio piece.
Use the Pomodoro technique (25/5) to keep focus during your 7-hour days and take longer breaks mid-day.
Write short daily notes: what you learned, what was hard, and one question to resolve next session — this builds momentum and clarifies blockers.
Prioritize building and shipping small working increments early; running code and tests beats much passive reading.
Reserve the last 2 weeks of Month 3 for polishing the capstone and interview practice (mock interviews, explaining your architecture).
